64:9.ar: يَوۡمَ يَجۡمَعُكُمۡ لِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡجَمۡعِۖ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلتَّغَابُنِۗ وَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ وَيَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحࣰ ا يُكَفِّرۡ عَنۡهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِۦ وَيُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
64:9.en: The day when He shall gather you unto the Day of Assembling, that will be a day of mutual disillusion. And whoso believeth in Allah and doeth right, He will remit from him his evil deeds and will bring him unto Gardens underneath which rivers flow, therein to abide for ever. That is the supreme triumph

64:10.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
64:10.en: But those who disbelieve and deny Our revelations, such are owners of the Fire; they will abide therein - a hapless journey's end

64:11.ar: مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ يَهۡدِ قَلۡبَهُۥۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
64:11.en: No calamity befalleth save by Allah's leave. And whosoever believeth in Allah, He guideth his heart. And Allah is Knower of all things

64:12.ar: وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَۚ فَإِن تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَىٰ رَسُولِنَا ٱلۡبَلَٰغُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
64:12.en: Obey Allah and obey His messenger; but if ye turn away, then the duty of Our messenger is only to convey (the message) plainly

64:13.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
64:13.en: Allah! There is no Allah save Him. In Allah, therefore, let believers put their trust

64:14.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡ عَدُوࣰّ ا لَّكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُمۡۚ وَإِن تَعۡفُواْ وَتَصۡفَحُواْ وَتَغۡفِرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
64:14.en: O ye who believe! Lo! among your wives and your children there are enemies for you, therefor beware of them. And if ye efface and overlook and forgive, then lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

9:118.ar: وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلَٰثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُواْ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَن لَّا مَلۡجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لِيَتُوبُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
9:118.en: And to the three also (did He turn in mercy) who were left behind, when the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for them, and their own souls were straitened for them till they bethought them that there is no refuge from Allah save toward Him. Then turned He unto them in mercy that they (too) might turn (repentant unto Him). Lo! Allah! He is the Relenting, the Merciful

35:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ فَٱتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّاۚ إِنَّمَا يَدۡعُواْ حِزۡبَهُۥ لِيَكُونُواْ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
35:6.en: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire

vN2CM_SD6Ek.title: Surat Al-Taghabun, Part 3 (Verses 9-14)
vN2CM_SD6Ek.one_line: Al-Taghabun 9-14: the Day self-deception ends, calamity and a guided heart, obedience, tawakkul, and forgiving family who act like enemies.
vN2CM_SD6Ek.summary: He returns to verse 9 to stress the surah's role among technical Medinan surahs: when people forget why they practise, rituals become identity and the community splinters. The Day of Taghabun strips away the stories people tell themselves to live with their wrongs, and only those who refined their intentions will find their true motives flattering. He illustrates with giving advice: doing it to feel right versus doing it so the person benefits. Verses 11 to 13 he calls a road map for life. First, every calamity happens by Allah's permission, which includes free will and the order of nature, and pain is what gives ease its meaning; keep your iman so your heart stays guided, because loss is only real when you stop moving. He points to the Prophet at Ta'if and to the eighteen close family members he buried while still smiling. Second, obey Allah and His Messenger, whose only duty was to convey clearly. Third, there is no god but Allah, so rely fully on Him. He defines tawakkul as doing your full part, trusting Allah with the result and accepting whatever comes, which makes believers bold. Verse 14 warns that spouses and children may act like enemies; beware of letting them take away your reason for serving them, and instead pardon, overlook and forgive.

outline.heading: Three dimensions of a surah
outline.gist: Know when it was revealed and where it sits among its neighbours; the third dimension is what you take from it.

outline.heading: Losing the why breeds sectarianism
outline.gist: Amid technical Medinan rulings, forgetting why you act turns the action into identity, kills flexibility and divides groups; this surah is a pause to restore the why.

outline.heading: The Day of Taghabun: the day all deceit ends
outline.gist: Taghabun is mutual fooling, and the name can carry its opposite: the day when no one can fool anyone, including oneself.

outline.heading: The stories we tell ourselves to sleep at night
outline.gist: Oppressors and abusers build narratives that let them live with themselves; on that Day those narratives vanish and only reality remains.

outline.heading: 'Amila salihan: the deeds you are needed for
outline.gist: Righteous work means the deed suited to people's real needs, at the right time and proportion; teaching starving people to pray while ignoring hunger avoids the harder work of reform.

outline.heading: Rivers flowing beneath: self-sufficiency in Paradise
outline.gist: Water from under your own land signals independence; the Quran describes psychological comfort in Jannah as much as physical pleasure.

outline.heading: Kafaru wa kadhdhabu: rejecting a truth you recognize
outline.gist: The punished are those who saw the truth and refused it for selfish reasons, unlike those never reached properly with da'wah; never hope anyone is denied Paradise.

outline.heading: No sugarcoating on that Day
outline.gist: Our true reasons are rarely flattering unless we spent a lifetime refining our intentions and asking whom we are pleasing.

outline.heading: Advice: for your sake or for theirs?
outline.gist: Correcting someone can serve your ego by embarrassing them, or serve them by choosing the right time, person and manner; people avoid the masjid because of nosy corrections.

outline.heading: The man who raised his left finger
outline.gist: A scholar eager to correct a man pointing with his left hand in tashahhud found he had no right index finger; ask whether you want to give advice or want the person to benefit.

outline.heading: Never lose the why; the end of those who turn away
outline.gist: Uphold every ruling, but once the why is gone rulings get used to harm; those who reject after clarity face the worst destiny.

outline.heading: Interlude
Jazm in the conditional: yahdi qalbahu
outline.gist: The condition holds the verb captive, which is why its final letter drops.

outline.heading: Interlude
It is fine to call a calamity a calamity
outline.gist: A musibah is judged by how it feels when it happens; you need not call it a blessing at the time, only deal with it rightly.

outline.heading: Moments of suffocation, and how the Prophet reacted
outline.gist: Everyone faces times when the chest tightens; the Prophet felt sorrow too, but his confidence in Allah never shook.

outline.heading: Ta'if: the hardest day and having no plan
outline.gist: Asked his hardest day, the Prophet named the walk back from Ta'if with no plan; as a physician he notes how much a plan matters, and the Prophet turned to Allah in his famous dua.

outline.heading: Bi-idhnillah: permission is not approval
outline.gist: Allah permitted free will and the workings of nature, so harm from people and nature happens within His permission without pleasing Him.

outline.heading: Things are known by their opposites
outline.gist: Without sour there is no sweet, and a rock cannot be sick or happy; joy and health only mean something because pain and illness exist.

outline.heading: A guided heart: you lose only when you stop moving
outline.gist: Accept that calamity was accounted for, keep your iman so your heart stays guided, and get up again; defeat is when calamity takes your faith.

outline.heading: The Prophet's eighteen losses
outline.gist: He buried parents, grandfather, uncles, aunts, children, wives and an adopted son, mourned them all his life, yet kept smiling with grace.

outline.heading: Second statement: obey Allah and the Messenger
outline.gist: Revelation and the Prophet's practice are one source in two layers; obedience is complex, and the Messenger's only duty was clear conveyance, so turning away harms only you.

outline.heading: Third statement: no god but Him, so rely on Him
outline.gist: The three verses are a remedy for anyone lost or struggling.

outline.heading: Three reasons for gratitude in calamity
outline.gist: A companion would be grateful that it was not worse, remember that his true loss was the Prophet, and thank Allah it did not touch his religion.

outline.heading: The why: no one else is worthy
outline.gist: No one deserves your devotion, freedom or sacrifice but Allah; you honour parents and obey the law because He asks you to.

outline.heading: Tawakkul defined: effort, dependence, acceptance
outline.gist: Do your full part, know outcomes come from Allah, and when the result does not come, do not let it take your iman; try again or change direction.

outline.heading: Tawakkul makes believers brave
outline.gist: Playing it safe is trying to control the outcome; tawakkul allows calculated risks.

outline.heading: Interlude
Enemies among your spouses and children
outline.gist: Those you dedicate your life to serving may act against your interest, which is very hard to accept.

outline.heading: Beware of what? Of losing your why
outline.gist: You serve your family for Allah, not for them, so beware of their behaviour taking away your intention and making you sink the ship.

outline.heading: The occasions behind the verse
outline.gist: Families who held men back from expeditions or hijrah, and children who left Islam and turned on their parents.

outline.heading: Pardon, overlook, forgive
outline.gist: Forgive the sin, overlook the sinner and conceal the matter rather than exposing it; Shaytan is the one to treat as an enemy.

outline.heading: The hardest verse: when the betrayal is at home
outline.gist: A man endures the world for his family, and betrayal from within feels like it makes life worthless; keep preserving the family for Allah's sake rather than destroying it.

outline.heading: Outro

6:162.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحۡيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
6:162.en: Say: Lo! my worship and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the Worlds

6:163.ar: لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُۥۖ وَبِذَٰلِكَ أُمِرۡتُ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
6:163.en: He hath no partner. This am I commanded, and I am first of those who surrender (unto Him)

12:91.ar: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدۡ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
12:91.en: They said: By Allah, verily Allah hath preferred thee above us, and we were indeed sinful

12:92.ar: قَالَ لَا تَثۡرِيبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ يَغۡفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
12:92.en: He said: Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy

73:1.en: O thou wrapped up in thy raiment

73:2.en: Keep vigil the night long, save a little

74:1.en: O thou enveloped in thy cloak

34:46.ar: ۞قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٰحِدَةٍۖ أَن تَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُواْۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍۚ إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ لَّكُم بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ عَذَابࣲ شَدِيدࣲ‏
34:46.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I exhort you unto one thing only: that ye awake, for Allah's sake, by twos and singly, and then reflect: There is no madness in your comrade. He is naught else than a warner unto you in face of a terrific doom

9:90.ar: وَجَآءَ ٱلۡمُعَذِّرُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابِ لِيُؤۡذَنَ لَهُمۡ وَقَعَدَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَبُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۚ سَيُصِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
9:90.en: And those among the wandering Arabs who had an excuse came in order that permission might be granted them. And those who lied to Allah and His messenger sat at home. A painful doom will fall on those of them who disbelieve

9:86.ar: وَإِذَآ أُنزِلَتۡ سُورَةٌ أَنۡ ءَامِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَجَٰهِدُواْ مَعَ رَسُولِهِ ٱسۡتَـٔۡذَنَكَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلطَّوۡلِ مِنۡهُمۡ وَقَالُواْ ذَرۡنَا نَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡقَٰعِدِينَ
9:86.en: And when a surah is revealed (which saith): Believe in Allah and strive along with His messenger, the men of wealth among them still ask leave of thee and say: Suffer us to be with those who sit (at home)

18:9.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتَ أَنَّ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡكَهۡفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُواْ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا
18:9.en: Or deemest thou that the People of the Cave and the Inscription are a wonder among Our portents

18:17.ar: ۞وَتَرَى ٱلشَّمۡسَ إِذَا طَلَعَت تَّزَٰوَرُ عَن كَهۡفِهِمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَت تَّقۡرِضُهُمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ وَهُمۡ فِي فَجۡوَةࣲ مِّنۡهُۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِۗ مَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِۖ وَمَن يُضۡلِلۡ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُۥ وَلِيࣰّ ا مُّرۡشِدࣰ ا
18:17.en: And thou mightest have seen the sun when it rose move away from their cave to the right, and when it set go past them on the left, and they were in the cleft thereof. That was (one) of the portents of Allah. He whom Allah guideth, he indeed is led aright, and he whom He sendeth astray, for him thou wilt not find a guiding friend

18:14.ar: وَرَبَطۡنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ إِذۡ قَامُواْ فَقَالُواْ رَبُّنَا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَن نَّدۡعُوَاْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَٰهࣰ اۖ لَّقَدۡ قُلۡنَآ إِذࣰ ا شَطَطًا
18:14.en: And We made firm their hearts when they stood forth and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We cry unto no Allah beside Him, for then should we utter an enormity

18:19.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ بَعَثۡنَٰهُمۡ لِيَتَسَآءَلُواْ بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ قَالَ قَآئِلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتُمۡۖ قَالُواْ لَبِثۡنَا يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲۚ قَالُواْ رَبُّكُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثۡتُمۡ فَٱبۡعَثُوٓاْ أَحَدَكُم بِوَرِقِكُمۡ هَٰذِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ فَلۡيَنظُرۡ أَيُّهَآ أَزۡكَىٰ طَعَامࣰ ا فَلۡيَأۡتِكُم بِرِزۡقࣲ مِّنۡهُ وَلۡيَتَلَطَّفۡ وَلَا يُشۡعِرَنَّ بِكُمۡ أَحَدًا
18:19.en: And in like manner We awakened them that they might question one another. A speaker from among them said: How long have ye tarried? They said: We have tarried a day or some part of a day, (Others) said: Your Lord best knoweth what ye have tarried. Now send one of you with this your silver coin unto the city, and let him see what food is purest there and bring you a supply thereof. Let him be courteous and let no man know of you

uJh24LKEQds.title: Activism, Our Path Forward 1
uJh24LKEQds.one_line: Islam means qiyam, standing up for a cause with your whole life, as the Prophet did and as the youths of the cave did.
uJh24LKEQds.summary: He defines activism, a word with no exact Arabic equivalent, as dedicating every part of your life to a cause beyond yourself, with devotion, simple living and understanding. His verse is 'my prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for Allah'. Muslims have turned the tables, staying humble about religion and ambitious about money; ambition belongs in faith, to be among the best of Muslims, treating the world as a stop on a journey. The Prophet personified the verse and was never at rest. At Hudaybiyyah he vowed to keep going until the faith prevailed or he died; he forgave Abu Sufyan with the words of Yusuf, and onlookers said kings are feared but he was loved. He won hearts through relentless dedication, not force. The Quran's word for this is qiyam, standing, while those who refused are described as sitting. In the Arabic second khutbah he says the default in Islam is taking a stand for truth and against injustice, not giving a few hours and some money while aiming only to scrape into Paradise. Al-Kahf is read weekly for its story: three teenagers and a dog stood against a tyrant, and Allah woke them after 300 years to see their spark had changed the land. Do your part; outcomes belong to Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Activism: a word with no Arabic equivalent
outline.gist: Islam has the concept, but look for an Arabic translation of 'activism' and you will find nothing anyone has ever used in a sentence.

outline.heading: A whole life directed to a cause beyond yourself
outline.gist: Activists dedicate their lives to a cause beyond themselves, a social injustice, a human right or a reform, so that every aspect of life serves that goal. It takes devotion, a minimalist lifestyle and understanding.

outline.heading: The verse as the activist's creed
outline.gist: He returns to 'my prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, with no partner; this I was commanded': a life in which everything is directed to one cause.

outline.heading: Humble in religion, ambitious about money
outline.gist: Muslims are humble about religion and ambitious about money and success; the tables have turned. Be ambitious in faith, aiming to be the best Muslim and get there first, as a matter of effort, not superiority or arrogance.

outline.heading: Aspire to the companions' pledge
outline.gist: Aspire to be like the companions, who pledged to the Prophet on the shahadah, establishing prayer, paying zakat and sincere advice to every Muslim.

outline.heading: The world as a rider's resting place
outline.gist: Like a rider who rests in the shade and moves on, treat the world as a stop on the way to a destination. Wanting the biggest house and the best car is a mindset that leaves us, as individuals and communities, in deep trouble.

outline.heading: The Prophet never rested
outline.gist: Those who saw him knew he owned nothing great, yet he was never at rest, because he had to personify 'my prayer and my rites, my living and my dying'.

outline.heading: Hudaybiyyah: until Allah makes it prevail or I die
outline.gist: Living that way is very difficult but not impossible. When Quraysh kept sending people to provoke him at Hudaybiyyah, he said war had exhausted them and he would not leave this matter until Allah made it prevail or his neck was severed; no obstacle or betrayal stopped him.

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan forgiven with Yusuf's words
outline.gist: Abu Sufyan, long an opponent, came to repent with his family and was told to say what Yusuf's brothers said, 'Allah has preferred you over us'. The Prophet, always looking for a chance to live the Quran, answered at once: 'No blame on you today; may Allah forgive you.'

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan weeps: 'how forbearing you are'
outline.gist: Urged to say la ilaha illa Allah, Abu Sufyan wept and said, 'How forbearing, how generous, how kind to kin you are': he could not beat this man and did not know why.

outline.heading: Kings are feared; he was loved
outline.gist: An envoy who watched the companions catch the water of his wudu went back and said he had seen kings, but none like this. Kings are feared and flattered out of fear; Muhammad was loved.

outline.heading: He beat them with relentless dedication
outline.gist: Living without rest, giving up home and comfort and asking nothing in return is what changes hearts. He beat his opponents not with force but with relentless dedication, thanking those who helped and carrying on without those who did not.

outline.heading: Respect that took months to become faith
outline.gist: Abu Sufyan said the shahadah out of respect for a dedication he had never seen, and only months later did his heart fill with it. The Prophet's whole life and death were for Allah.

outline.heading: The Quran's word: qum, stand
outline.gist: The Quran's word for this is standing: 'O you wrapped, arise', 'O you cloaked, arise and warn', and 'stand for Allah in pairs and alone, then reflect'.

outline.heading: Those who refused sat back
outline.gist: Those who lied to Allah and His Messenger are described as sitting, and when told to strive with the Messenger the wealthy asked to stay with those who sit.

outline.heading: He never took a holiday from dawah
outline.gist: The Prophet had no rest in his life: he strove for Allah as is His due and never took a day of ease or a month's leave from calling people.

outline.heading: The default in Islam is qiyam
outline.gist: He stayed standing at his work until death, and that is the Muslim's way. Qiyam is not standing on your feet but taking a stand: seeing truth and supporting it, seeing falsehood or injustice and working to remove it.

outline.heading: A few hours and some money, and endless worldly ambition
outline.gist: A Muslim cannot give Allah a few hours and some money while hoping just to scrape into the edge of Paradise, with worldly ambitions that never end: a bigger house, a bigger car, more wives. No righteous person or companion lived that way.

outline.heading: Lowly aspiration will not reach their station
outline.gist: Those who reached the highest ranks made Allah their focus and devoted themselves sincerely to Him, and still feared their deeds would not be accepted. Indifference to the Hereafter with greed for the world will help no one on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Why Al-Kahf is read every week
outline.gist: He fears for himself more than for anyone, but the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous did not live this way; to reach them, live like them. Al-Kahf is recited every week, though some dislike it, because the story it is named after must be understood.

outline.heading: Change needs people dedicated to an idea
outline.gist: No other surah gets this treatment. Change needs people dedicated to an idea; coming once a week, listening and leaving changes nothing in the world.

outline.heading: Carved up like a pie
outline.gist: When the ummah fell it was cut up like a pie and its holy land given to people who do not belong there. Weekly attendance will not change that; it takes people willing to live and die for a cause.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:9: the cave and the raqim
outline.gist: 'Did you think the people of the cave and the raqim were a wonder among Our signs?' Raqim means both their village and a tablet on which they wrote their principles, goals and mission.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:17: the One who did it then can do it now
outline.gist: The sun turning away from their cave was a sign, but Allah does not change: the One who did it then can do it now. The question is whether there are people of the cave today.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:14: hearts strengthened when they stood
outline.gist: Allah strengthened their hearts when they stood up; they dedicated themselves to a cause and saw staying seated as no option. Islam is not a buffet you pick from.

outline.heading: Three teenagers and a dog against a tyrant
outline.gist: Three teenagers and a dog believed they could change a country and a political system ruled by a dictator claiming to be god, and worked for it for a couple of months.

outline.heading: Waking after 300 years to see their spark
outline.gist: Why sleep 300 years and wake for twelve hours? Allah woke them to show them what their effort did: the revolution that removed the tyrant took generations, but their spark lit it.

outline.heading: Their faces on the currency: just do your job
outline.gist: Their coin was 300 years out of date and the new currency bore their faces. You do not know how the world works; do your job, follow the teaching and exhaust your resources.

outline.heading: Outcomes are Allah's; a masjid over them
outline.gist: Be wise, but the outcomes are in Allah's hands alone. Those who prevailed over their matter said they would build a masjid over them.

outline.heading: Outro

28:30.ar: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِيَ مِن شَٰطِيِٕ ٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنِ فِي ٱلۡبُقۡعَةِ ٱلۡمُبَٰرَكَةِ مِنَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ أَن يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
28:30.en: And when he reached it, he was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed field, from the tree: O Moses! Lo! I, even I, am Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

28:31.ar: وَأَنۡ أَلۡقِ عَصَاكَۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهۡتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنࣱّ وَلَّىٰ مُدۡبِرࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يُعَقِّبۡۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقۡبِلۡ وَلَا تَخَفۡۖ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓمِنِينَ
28:31.en: Throw down thy staff. And when he saw it writhing as it had been a demon, he turned to flee headlong, (and it was said unto him): O Moses! Draw nigh and fear not. Lo! thou art of those who are secure

28:32.ar: ٱسۡلُكۡ يَدَكَ فِي جَيۡبِكَ تَخۡرُجۡ بَيۡضَآءَ مِنۡ غَيۡرِ سُوٓءࣲ وَٱضۡمُمۡ إِلَيۡكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهۡبِۖ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرۡهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
28:32.en: Thrust thy hand into the bosom of thy robe it will come forth white without hurt. And guard thy heart from fear. Then these shall be two proofs from your Lord unto Pharaoh and his chiefs. Lo! they are evil-living folk

28:33.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي قَتَلۡتُ مِنۡهُمۡ نَفۡسࣰ ا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقۡتُلُونِ
28:33.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I killed a man among them and I fear that they will kill me

28:34.ar: وَأَخِي هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفۡصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانࣰ ا فَأَرۡسِلۡهُ مَعِيَ رِدۡءࣰ ا يُصَدِّقُنِيٓۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
28:34.en: My brother Aaron is more eloquent than me in speech. Therefor send him with me as a helper to confirm me. Lo! I fear that they will give the lie to me

20:21.ar: قَالَ خُذۡهَا وَلَا تَخَفۡۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلۡأُولَىٰ
20:21.en: He said: Grasp it and fear not. We shall return it to its former state

18:17.ar: ۞وَتَرَى ٱلشَّمۡسَ إِذَا طَلَعَت تَّزَٰوَرُ عَن كَهۡفِهِمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَت تَّقۡرِضُهُمۡ ذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ وَهُمۡ فِي فَجۡوَةࣲ مِّنۡهُۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِۗ مَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِۖ وَمَن يُضۡلِلۡ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُۥ وَلِيࣰّ ا مُّرۡشِدࣰ ا
18:17.en: And thou mightest have seen the sun when it rose move away from their cave to the right, and when it set go past them on the left, and they were in the cleft thereof. That was (one) of the portents of Allah. He whom Allah guideth, he indeed is led aright, and he whom He sendeth astray, for him thou wilt not find a guiding friend

5:46.ar: وَقَفَّيۡنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم بِعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡإِنجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدࣰ ى وَنُورࣱ وَمُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَهُدࣰ ى وَمَوۡعِظَةࣰ لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
5:46.en: And We caused Jesus, son of Mary, to follow in their footsteps, confirming that which was (revealed) before him in the Torah, and We bestowed on him the Gospel wherein is guidance and a light, confirming that which was (revealed) before it in the Torah - a guidance and an admonition unto those who ward off (evil)

20:46.ar: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآۖ إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَآ أَسۡمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
20:46.en: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing

20:25.en: (Moses) said: My Lord! relieve my mind

20:26.en: And ease my task for me

20:27.en: And loose a knot from my tongue

20:28.en: That they may understand my saying

20:29.ar: وَٱجۡعَل لِّي وَزِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِي
20:29.en: Appoint for me a henchman from my folk

20:32.en: And let him share my task

20:43.en: Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds)

20:44.ar: فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوۡلࣰ ا لَّيِّنࣰ ا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوۡ يَخۡشَىٰ
20:44.en: And speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed or fear

79:18.ar: فَقُلۡ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
79:18.en: And say (unto him): Hast thou (will) to grow (in grace)

79:19.en: Then I will guide thee to thy Lord and thou shalt fear (Him)

Nfz6ey3N8os.speaker_note: continues his Friday Arabic tafsir of al-Qasas from verse 30, recapping the series
Nfz6ey3N8os.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat al-Qasas, the Signs and the Mission (28:30-35)
Nfz6ey3N8os.one_line: Musa's call and signs: dealing with Allah rather than people, why reformers are honoured, the decisive proof, and strengthening your brother.
Nfz6ey3N8os.summary: Before resuming the verses he reflects on why Musa was chosen. He refused power with Pharaoh and paid dearly, losing home and family, yet never turned on his people, because he was dealing with Allah, not with them. Whoever acts for Allah expects no thanks or return; if you want something back, state it openly, which he applies to marriage: put expectations in the agreement, or give purely for Allah and refuse repayment, so resentment does not grow and ruin the home. The Prophet sought no praise, unlike poets who flattered kings for money. Those who strive to reform their people deserve to be spoken to by Allah, while retreating into a comfortable private life is not an option for a Muslim, since the whole ship sinks together. He then explains the staff that moves like a darting snake, the shining hand, and why these are a decisive proof that the magicians recognised at once. Allah spoke to Musa directly, without Jibril, because of the magnitude of confronting the greatest tyrant alone. Musa honestly admits his fear and halting speech and asks for Harun to strengthen him; a true brother is one through whom your arm is strengthened. The promise that the enemy will not reach them is a promise of prevailing in argument, and our own decisive miracle is the Quran, which Muslims neglect.

outline.heading: Recap: our relationship with people's stories
outline.gist: Al-Qasas, the longest surah of the axis, teaches that we know others only through the stories told about them.

outline.heading: Returning after the years in Madyan
outline.gist: Likely he served ten years so the case would lapse with time; he returned feeling safe from trial though still wary.

outline.heading: Allah shows why He chose His prophets
outline.gist: Ibrahim was given guidance before, Dawud kingship after Goliath; each was qualified by character before being chosen.

outline.heading: Istifa: choosing and raising rank
outline.gist: Musa refused power and suffered for it; keeping to Allah's path can bring hardship, and people struggle with this.

outline.heading: Yusuf chosen after refusing temptation
outline.gist: Yusuf's prophethood came at the end of his story; patience with Allah's will does not earn ease in this life, the ease comes on the Day.

outline.heading: He lost everything and did not complain
outline.gist: His own people caused his exile, his mother died before his return, yet he never said they had wronged him; Allah does not change toward those who deal with Him.

outline.heading: You deal with Allah, not with people
outline.gist: Had he served his people only out of love he would have turned away after what they did; beware of the one you did good to.

outline.heading: Expect nothing, or say what you want upfront
outline.gist: If you act for Allah, any return should even worry you; if you want something, a vote, loyalty, support, say so openly, which is not shameful.

outline.heading: Musa's character was the same everywhere
outline.gist: Neither haughty in Egypt nor servile in Madyan; this is why he was honoured with prophethood.

outline.heading: In marriage, put expectations in the agreement
outline.gist: If you want something in return for taking on extra roles, agree it in advance, such as sharing housework for sharing income.

outline.heading: Doing it for Allah means refusing a return
outline.gist: The husband provides and the wife runs the home; if one takes on the other's role, there must be balance, or it is done purely for Allah.

outline.heading: The Prophet sought no thanks
outline.gist: Poets praised kings for money and lost their dignity; Musa, Yusuf and Muhammad wanted nothing from their people and so did not abandon them.

outline.heading: Resentment that ruins homes
outline.gist: Unspoken expectations breed small grudges that grow and spoil love between spouses.

outline.heading: Reformers deserve to be addressed by Allah
outline.gist: Musa returned intending to free his people, and that intention made him worthy; find this intention in your own heart.

outline.heading: The companions tempted to settle in Madinah
outline.gist: Once life stabilised, some felt they could rest, but the aim remained taking Islam to all and ending tyranny.

outline.heading: Private comfort is not an option
outline.gist: You cannot just raise your children and ignore the ummah; a tidy cabin on the upper deck sinks with the ship.

outline.heading: Created sound, eternal speech; reciting jann
outline.gist: Recap of the creed point, and the ten counts in reciting 'jann'.

outline.heading: Recitation: the hand and the arm
outline.gist: In Hafs 'rahb' is read with a sukun here, unlike other readings.

outline.heading: The staff becomes a darting snake
outline.gist: Jann means something moving uncontrollably; a wooden staff turned into a living snake and an unknown voice spoke, so he fled in fear.

outline.heading: Security and the shining hand
outline.gist: Messengers need not fear before Allah; the jayb is the neck opening, and the hand came out dazzling white with no disease.

outline.heading: Draw in your arm against fear
outline.gist: Janah is the upper arm, like a wing under wide sleeves; 'dhanika' marks two proofs addressed to Musa.

outline.heading: A burhan admits no other reading
outline.gist: A decisive proof is understood one way, like the clear verses of the Book; the magicians recognised it at once, prostrated and died rather than retract.

outline.heading: Why Allah spoke without Jibril
outline.gist: Allah removed the intermediary because of the magnitude of what Musa was undertaking, and gave him proofs rather than instructions.

outline.heading: Allah honours those who rise for their people
outline.gist: Like the youths of the cave, Musa, alone and poor, set out to challenge the greatest tyrant, and Allah honoured him by speaking to him.

outline.heading: Intend what Musa intended
outline.gist: Think of the tyrant in the land you came from; many of us live here because we could not stand up to ours.

outline.heading: I fear they will kill me: recitation and rawm
outline.gist: At the verse ends one may voice a third of the kasrah with rawm, under specific conditions.

outline.heading: Raising awareness of the readings
outline.gist: Al-Fatihah has three readings of 'sirat'; people need more awareness so other readings do not confuse them.

outline.heading: Musa's honesty about his weaknesses
outline.gist: His fear was now of revenge, not trial; he admitted Harun was more eloquent.

outline.heading: So he can confirm me
outline.gist: Tasdiq here means supporting the truth of Musa's message, as the Gospel confirms the Torah.

outline.heading: Musa's prayer for his brother
outline.gist: His first thought on receiving prophethood was for his brother to share it; shameful that in this ummah brothers stop speaking.

outline.heading: We will strengthen your arm: valid pauses
outline.gist: Pausing at 'to you two' or at 'by Our signs' are both correct.

outline.heading: A brother strengthens your arm
outline.gist: If you do not strengthen your brother you are not a brother; Musa said plainly what was in his heart.

outline.heading: They will not reach you: prevailing in argument
outline.gist: Not a guarantee of life but that no enemy will defeat their proof; the Prophet's greatest miracle is the Quran.

outline.heading: Muslims turning away from the Quran
outline.gist: With the greatest miracle in hand, our neglect of the Quran is strange.

outline.heading: Musa returns; Harun goes out to meet him
outline.gist: His mother had died; Jibril told Harun of the mission, and both were sent to speak gently to Pharaoh.

outline.heading: Outro

20:118.ar: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعۡرَىٰ
20:118.en: It is (vouchsafed) unto thee that thou hungerest not therein nor art naked

20:119.ar: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظۡمَؤُاْ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضۡحَىٰ
20:119.en: And that thou thirstest not therein nor art exposed to the sun's heat

20:120.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكࣲ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ
20:120.en: But the devil whispered to him, saying: O Adam! Shall I show thee the tree of immortality and power that wasteth not away

7:22.ar: فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورࣲۚ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتۡ لَهُمَا سَوۡءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخۡصِفَانِ عَلَيۡهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمۡ أَنۡهَكُمَا عَن تِلۡكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
7:22.en: Thus did he lead them on with guile. And when they tasted of the tree their shame was manifest to them and they began to hide (by heaping) on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And their Lord called them, (saying): Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you: Lo! Satan is an open enemy to you

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

7:172.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَأَشۡهَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ شَهِدۡنَآۚ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَٰذَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:172.en: And (remember) when thy Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their reins, their seed, and made them testify of themselves, (saying): Am I not your Lord? They said: Yea, verily. We testify. (That was) lest ye should say at the Day of Resurrection: Lo! of this we were unaware

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him. Lo! He is the relenting, the Merciful

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast

21:52.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
21:52.en: When he said unto his father and his folk: What are these images unto which ye pay devotion

6:76.ar: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلَّيۡلُ رَءَا كَوۡكَبࣰ اۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَآ أُحِبُّ ٱلۡأٓفِلِينَ
6:76.en: When the night grew dark upon him he beheld a star. He said: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: I love not things that set

6:77.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡقَمَرَ بَازِغࣰ ا قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَئِن لَّمۡ يَهۡدِنِي رَبِّي لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
6:77.en: And when he saw the moon uprising, he exclaimed: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: Unless my Lord guide me, I surely shall become one of the folk who are astray

6:78.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ بَازِغَةࣰ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّي هَٰذَآ أَكۡبَرُۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَتۡ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّي بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّمَّا تُشۡرِكُونَ
6:78.en: And when he saw the sun uprising, he cried: This is my Lord! This is greater! And when it set he exclaimed: O my people! Lo! I am free from all that ye associate (with Him)

2:258.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ فِي رَبِّهِۦٓ أَنۡ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ إِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّيَ ٱلَّذِي يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ أُحۡيِۦ وَأُمِيتُۖ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡتِي بِٱلشَّمۡسِ مِنَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ فَأۡتِ بِهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:258.en: Bethink thee of him who had an argument with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him the kingdom; how, when Abraham said: My Lord is He Who giveth life and causeth death, he answered: I give life and cause death. Abraham said: Lo! Allah causeth the sun to rise in the East, so do thou cause it to come up from the West. Thus was the disbeliever abashed. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

37:103.en: Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face

37:104.en: We called unto him: O Abraham

37:105.ar: قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
37:105.en: Thou hast already fulfilled the vision. Lo! thus do We reward the good

37:106.en: Lo! that verily was a clear test

37:107.en: Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim

47:36.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱۚ وَإِن تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ أُجُورَكُمۡ وَلَا يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمۡ
47:36.en: The life of the world is but a sport and a pastime. And if ye believe and ward off (evil). He will give you your wages, and will not ask of you your wordly wealth

47:37.ar: إِن يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمُوهَا فَيُحۡفِكُمۡ تَبۡخَلُواْ وَيُخۡرِجۡ أَضۡغَٰنَكُمۡ
47:37.en: If He should ask it of you and importune you, ye would hoard it, and He would bring to light your (secret) hates

47:38.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ تُدۡعَوۡنَ لِتُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَمِنكُم مَّن يَبۡخَلُۖ وَمَن يَبۡخَلۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَبۡخَلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوٓاْ أَمۡثَٰلَكُم
47:38.en: Lo! ye are those who are called to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you there are some who hoard. And as for him who hoardeth, he hoardeth only from his soul. And Allah is the Rich, and ye are the poor. And if ye turn away He will exchange you for some other folk, and they will not be the likes of you

14:37.ar: رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّيٓ أَسۡكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيۡرِ ذِي زَرۡعٍ عِندَ بَيۡتِكَ ٱلۡمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجۡعَلۡ أَفۡـِٔدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَٱرۡزُقۡهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡكُرُونَ
14:37.en: Our Lord! Lo! I have settled some of my posterity in an uncultivable valley near unto Thy holy House, our Lord! that they may establish proper worship; so incline some hearts of men that they may yearn toward them, and provide Thou them with fruits in order that they may be thankful

18:25.ar: وَلَبِثُواْ فِي كَهۡفِهِمۡ ثَلَٰثَ مِاْئَةࣲ سِنِينَ وَٱزۡدَادُواْ تِسۡعࣰ ا
18:25.en: And (it is said) they tarried in their Cave three hundred years and add nine

5:3.ar: حُرِّمَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةُ وَٱلدَّمُ وَلَحۡمُ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡمُنۡخَنِقَةُ وَٱلۡمَوۡقُوذَةُ وَٱلۡمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيۡتُمۡ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسۡتَقۡسِمُواْ بِٱلۡأَزۡلَٰمِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ فِسۡقٌۗ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمۡ فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِۚ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ أَكۡمَلۡتُ لَكُمۡ دِينَكُمۡ وَأَتۡمَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعۡمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمَ دِينࣰ اۚ فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ فِي مَخۡمَصَةٍ غَيۡرَ مُتَجَانِفࣲ لِّإِثۡمࣲ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
5:3.en: Forbidden unto you (for food) are carrion and blood and swineflesh, and that which hath been dedicated unto any other than Allah, and the strangled, and the dead through beating, and the dead through falling from a height, and that which hath been killed by (the goring of) horns, and the devoured of wild beasts, saving that which ye make lawful (by the death-stroke), and that which hath been immolated unto idols. And (forbidden is it) that ye swear by the divining arrows. This is an abomination. This day are those who disbelieve in despair of (ever harming) your religion; so fear them not, fear Me! This day have I perfected your religion for you and completed My favour unto you, and have chosen for you as religion al-Islam. Whoso is forced by hunger, not by will, to sin: (for him) lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

K7Vrzpo80Ww.title: Arafah Program 2024: The Symbolism of Hajj
K7Vrzpo80Ww.one_line: On the night of Arafah he explains Hajj as walking in the footsteps of Adam and Hawwa, Ibrahim's family, and the Prophet with his nation.
K7Vrzpo80Ww.summary: He argues that Hajj seen mechanically, walking around rocks in a desert at great cost, makes little sense, but its symbolism is profound. He advises doing it once and well, since two billion Muslims compete for three million places. The highest level, from Ja'far al-Sadiq, sees only Allah: Arafah is His door, the Haram His yard, the Ka'bah His house. Then three tracks. Adam and Hawwa, separated after the fall that exposed flaws of character, recognized each other at Arafah, where humanity's covenant was taken; repented at Muzdalifah; wished for Paradise at Mina; stoned Iblis; and built the House, so standing at Arafah is a reunion of one human family. Ibrahim's family: Isma'il accepted the dream at Arafah, the three walked in submission through Muzdalifah, each stoned Iblis, and the knife did not cut; the sacrifice celebrates that Allah never commands what harms us, though we still resist the little He asks. Hajar's running teaches that effort, not outcome, is our job, as the youths of the cave learned. The Prophet's Hajj, through Jabir's account, ends with the completion of the religion, the charge to convey the message, and the question of what we will say about him.

outline.heading: Opening
The highest level: seeing only Allah
outline.gist: Few reach the level of Hajj where all one perceives is the relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: Hajj seen mechanically
outline.gist: Without its symbolism Hajj is walking around and between rocks in a desert, a poor investment.

outline.heading: Do Hajj once, and do it well
outline.gist: With two billion Muslims and three million places, repeating Hajj takes another's spot; in the past, travel from Syria or India was so hard that a full return was nearly a miracle.

outline.heading: Ja'far al-Sadiq: door, yard and house
outline.gist: Asked why Arafah lies outside the Haram, he explained the pilgrims stand at the door, enter the yard to perform the rites, then visit the house as guests who do not fast.

outline.heading: Three easier tracks of understanding
outline.gist: Hajj in the footsteps of Adam and Hawwa, of Ibrahim's family, and of the Prophet.

outline.heading: Adam's weaknesses: dying and being a servant
outline.gist: Given every comfort, Adam disliked death and servitude, and Iblis offered a tree of immortality and kingship.

outline.heading: The fall exposes flaws of character
outline.gist: What became apparent was not only their bodies but their lack of discipline; sent into harsh nature, they quarrelled and parted.

outline.heading: Recognition at Arafah
outline.gist: Searching and accepting responsibility, Adam saw Hawwa from a mountain and they knew each other and what they had done.

outline.heading: The covenant of Adam's offspring
outline.gist: Allah drew Adam's descendants and asked 'Am I not your Lord?', sending messengers to remind of it.

outline.heading: Standing where our parents stood
outline.gist: In two cloths with long hair you stand as Adam did; like visiting a loved one's places, it anchors you to a legacy.

outline.heading: A reunion of one human family
outline.gist: At least 25 nationalities in the room and millions at Arafah are siblings, none belonging to Adam more than another.

outline.heading: Knowing Allah, and repentance at Muzdalifah
outline.gist: The point of Arafah is knowing Allah; at Muzdalifah they drew close and repented with the words they were taught.

outline.heading: Mina: the wish to return to Paradise
outline.gist: Asked what he wished for, Adam hoped for Paradise and resolved to be better.

outline.heading: Stoning Iblis at the great jamrah
outline.gist: Devastated by Adam's repentance, Iblis returned and they stoned him until he disappeared.

outline.heading: Building the first House
outline.gist: Adam built while Hawwa carried rocks between Safa and Marwa; it was the first house for the first people.

outline.heading: Returning as on the day you were born
outline.gist: An accepted Hajj leaves behind not only sins but biases, grudges, trauma and bad habits.

outline.heading: The Ka'bah as a home, not a house
outline.gist: Bayt means home, the place you belong; you walk where your mother walked as she built it.

outline.heading: From a couple to a family to a nation
outline.gist: The tracks grow from Adam and Hawwa to Ibrahim's family to the Prophet and his ummah.

outline.heading: Isma'il at the age of striving
outline.gist: A son is carried, then works with you, then leaves, then carries you; Isma'il had reached the stage of helping his father.

outline.heading: The dream told at Arafah
outline.gist: Ibrahim told Isma'il at Arafah and both came to know what would come next.

outline.heading: How hard it is to accept one's death
outline.gist: Studies of death-row inmates show the dread as the date nears, showing the weight of what Isma'il accepted.

outline.heading: Muzdalifah: full submission and letting go
outline.gist: Accepting death requires letting go of what you cannot hold, like a curler releasing the stone, while staying responsible.

outline.heading: Hajar joins without a word
outline.gist: A mother whose husband was away most of the year accepted that her only son would be sacrificed.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the questioner
outline.gist: He questioned his father, the stars, the king and even Allah; parents should not expect children to obey without reasons.

outline.heading: No question this time
outline.gist: Told to sacrifice his son, Ibrahim asked nothing, because a clear command calls for submission.

outline.heading: Iblis tempts each of the three
outline.gist: Iblis urged Ibrahim, Hajar and Isma'il to refuse, and each stoned him, hence three jamarat.

outline.heading: The knife that did not cut
outline.gist: There was no bluff: Ibrahim struck, and the Lord of the knife stopped it.

outline.heading: The sacrifice celebrates Allah's mercy in His commands
outline.gist: Allah could have commanded harm, as with Ibrahim, but never does; His prohibitions all benefit us, yet we still disobey.

outline.heading: Asked for little, we still hold back
outline.gist: Allah asks only 2.5% of idle wealth, not all of it; whoever is stingy is stingy with himself (47:36-38).

outline.heading: A home is built by a family
outline.gist: Adam and Hawwa built it first, Ibrahim and Isma'il rebuilt it; the House was later lost under sand.

outline.heading: Hajar left in the valley
outline.gist: Ibrahim left her with a little water; she asked if Allah commanded it and said He would not abandon them.

outline.heading: Hajar's sa'y and Zamzam
outline.gist: She ran seven times between Safa and Marwa watching her son until Jibril struck the ground and water flowed.

outline.heading: Effort, not outcome, is your job
outline.gist: Sitting and waiting is unacceptable; you get what you strove for, like someone who dies while memorizing the Quran.

outline.heading: The youths of the cave
outline.gist: A few teenagers and a dog thought their stand achieved nothing; Allah woke them centuries later to show they changed their land.

outline.heading: Third track: the Prophet with his nation
outline.gist: Every stone of Makkah bears his footsteps; he performed Hajj once, three months before his death.

outline.heading: Jabir's account of the Farewell Hajj
outline.gist: The aged Jabir placed his hand on the young visitor's chest and narrated the longest authentic description of the Hajj.

outline.heading: A hundred thousand people walking in peace
outline.gist: Never had so many gathered outside war; people as far as the eye could see hoped to be near him.

outline.heading: The moment he most wishes to witness
outline.gist: He would choose to see the Prophet's face on that day, full of gratitude and humility.

outline.heading: From a cursed lone caller to the Mount of Mercy
outline.gist: Twenty years after being cursed by his uncle on a mountain, he stood before multitudes and named the mount.

outline.heading: Why millions stand on a barren mountain
outline.gist: There is no view or water, only rock, yet millions go because he stood there.

outline.heading: The religion completed
outline.gist: With 5:3, he knew his purpose was fulfilled and his death near, and he gave the Farewell Sermon.

outline.heading: Convey the message: later hearers may understand more
outline.gist: The final charge was meant for us: we can receive the message and do something even greater with it.

outline.heading: 'You will be asked about me'
outline.gist: The crowd fell silent, then testified he had conveyed it, and he took Allah as witness with tears.

outline.heading: Outro

22:29.ar: ثُمَّ لۡيَقۡضُواْ تَفَثَهُمۡ وَلۡيُوفُواْ نُذُورَهُمۡ وَلۡيَطَّوَّفُواْ بِٱلۡبَيۡتِ ٱلۡعَتِيقِ
22:29.en: Then let them make an end of their unkemptness and pay their vows and go around the ancient House

20:118.ar: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعۡرَىٰ
20:118.en: It is (vouchsafed) unto thee that thou hungerest not therein nor art naked

20:119.ar: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظۡمَؤُاْ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضۡحَىٰ
20:119.en: And that thou thirstest not therein nor art exposed to the sun's heat

20:120.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكࣲ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ
20:120.en: But the devil whispered to him, saying: O Adam! Shall I show thee the tree of immortality and power that wasteth not away

7:20.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِيُبۡدِيَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِيَ عَنۡهُمَا مِن سَوۡءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنۡ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيۡنِ أَوۡ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰلِدِينَ
7:20.en: Then Satan whispered to them that he might manifest unto them that which was hidden from them of their shame, and he said: Your Lord forbade you from this tree only lest ye should become angels or become of the immortals

7:21.en: And he swore unto them (saying): Lo! I am a sincere adviser unto you

7:22.ar: فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورࣲۚ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتۡ لَهُمَا سَوۡءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخۡصِفَانِ عَلَيۡهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمۡ أَنۡهَكُمَا عَن تِلۡكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
7:22.en: Thus did he lead them on with guile. And when they tasted of the tree their shame was manifest to them and they began to hide (by heaping) on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And their Lord called them, (saying): Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you: Lo! Satan is an open enemy to you

7:172.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَأَشۡهَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ شَهِدۡنَآۚ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَٰذَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:172.en: And (remember) when thy Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their reins, their seed, and made them testify of themselves, (saying): Am I not your Lord? They said: Yea, verily. We testify. (That was) lest ye should say at the Day of Resurrection: Lo! of this we were unaware

7:23.ar: قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمۡنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمۡ تَغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَتَرۡحَمۡنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
7:23.en: They said: Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If thou forgive us not and have not mercy on us, surely we are of the lost

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him. Lo! He is the relenting, the Merciful

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast

14:37.ar: رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّيٓ أَسۡكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيۡرِ ذِي زَرۡعٍ عِندَ بَيۡتِكَ ٱلۡمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجۡعَلۡ أَفۡـِٔدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَٱرۡزُقۡهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡكُرُونَ
14:37.en: Our Lord! Lo! I have settled some of my posterity in an uncultivable valley near unto Thy holy House, our Lord! that they may establish proper worship; so incline some hearts of men that they may yearn toward them, and provide Thou them with fruits in order that they may be thankful

6:76.ar: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلَّيۡلُ رَءَا كَوۡكَبࣰ اۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَآ أُحِبُّ ٱلۡأٓفِلِينَ
6:76.en: When the night grew dark upon him he beheld a star. He said: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: I love not things that set

6:77.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡقَمَرَ بَازِغࣰ ا قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَئِن لَّمۡ يَهۡدِنِي رَبِّي لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
6:77.en: And when he saw the moon uprising, he exclaimed: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: Unless my Lord guide me, I surely shall become one of the folk who are astray

6:78.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ بَازِغَةࣰ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّي هَٰذَآ أَكۡبَرُۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَتۡ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّي بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّمَّا تُشۡرِكُونَ
6:78.en: And when he saw the sun uprising, he cried: This is my Lord! This is greater! And when it set he exclaimed: O my people! Lo! I am free from all that ye associate (with Him)

21:52.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
21:52.en: When he said unto his father and his folk: What are these images unto which ye pay devotion

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the endeavour which is His right. He hath chosen you and hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship; the faith of your father Abraham (is yours). He hath named you Muslims of old time and in this (Scripture), that the messenger may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against mankind. So establish worship, pay the poor-due, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protecting friend. A blessed Patron and a blessed Helper

37:103.en: Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face

37:104.en: We called unto him: O Abraham

37:105.ar: قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
37:105.en: Thou hast already fulfilled the vision. Lo! thus do We reward the good

37:106.en: Lo! that verily was a clear test

37:107.en: Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim

47:36.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱۚ وَإِن تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ أُجُورَكُمۡ وَلَا يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمۡ
47:36.en: The life of the world is but a sport and a pastime. And if ye believe and ward off (evil). He will give you your wages, and will not ask of you your wordly wealth

47:37.ar: إِن يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمُوهَا فَيُحۡفِكُمۡ تَبۡخَلُواْ وَيُخۡرِجۡ أَضۡغَٰنَكُمۡ
47:37.en: If He should ask it of you and importune you, ye would hoard it, and He would bring to light your (secret) hates

47:38.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ تُدۡعَوۡنَ لِتُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَمِنكُم مَّن يَبۡخَلُۖ وَمَن يَبۡخَلۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَبۡخَلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوٓاْ أَمۡثَٰلَكُم
47:38.en: Lo! ye are those who are called to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you there are some who hoard. And as for him who hoardeth, he hoardeth only from his soul. And Allah is the Rich, and ye are the poor. And if ye turn away He will exchange you for some other folk, and they will not be the likes of you

2:127.ar: وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
2:127.en: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, (Abraham prayed): Our Lord! Accept from us (this duty). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer, the Knower

2:128.ar: رَبَّنَا وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا مُسۡلِمَيۡنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةࣰ مُّسۡلِمَةࣰ لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبۡ عَلَيۡنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:128.en: Our Lord! And make us submissive unto Thee and of our seed a nation submissive unto Thee, and show us our ways of worship, and relent toward us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Relenting, the Merciful

2:129.ar: رَبَّنَا وَٱبۡعَثۡ فِيهِمۡ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:129.en: Our Lord! And raise up in their midst a messenger from among them who shall recite unto them Thy revelations, and shall instruct them in the Scripture and in wisdom and shall make them grow. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Mighty, Wise

22:26.ar: وَإِذۡ بَوَّأۡنَا لِإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ مَكَانَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ أَن لَّا تُشۡرِكۡ بِي شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَطَهِّرۡ بَيۡتِيَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلۡقَآئِمِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
22:26.en: And (remember) when We prepared for Abraham the place of the (holy) House, saying: Ascribe thou no thing as partner unto Me, and purify My House for those who make the round (thereof) and those who stand and those who bow and make prostration

22:27.ar: وَأَذِّن فِي ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَجِّ يَأۡتُوكَ رِجَالࣰ ا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرࣲ يَأۡتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقࣲ‏
22:27.en: And proclaim unto mankind the pilgrimage. They will come unto thee on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep ravine

5:3.ar: حُرِّمَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةُ وَٱلدَّمُ وَلَحۡمُ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡمُنۡخَنِقَةُ وَٱلۡمَوۡقُوذَةُ وَٱلۡمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيۡتُمۡ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسۡتَقۡسِمُواْ بِٱلۡأَزۡلَٰمِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ فِسۡقٌۗ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمۡ فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِۚ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ أَكۡمَلۡتُ لَكُمۡ دِينَكُمۡ وَأَتۡمَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعۡمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمَ دِينࣰ اۚ فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ فِي مَخۡمَصَةٍ غَيۡرَ مُتَجَانِفࣲ لِّإِثۡمࣲ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
5:3.en: Forbidden unto you (for food) are carrion and blood and swineflesh, and that which hath been dedicated unto any other than Allah, and the strangled, and the dead through beating, and the dead through falling from a height, and that which hath been killed by (the goring of) horns, and the devoured of wild beasts, saving that which ye make lawful (by the death-stroke), and that which hath been immolated unto idols. And (forbidden is it) that ye swear by the divining arrows. This is an abomination. This day are those who disbelieve in despair of (ever harming) your religion; so fear them not, fear Me! This day have I perfected your religion for you and completed My favour unto you, and have chosen for you as religion al-Islam. Whoso is forced by hunger, not by will, to sin: (for him) lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

908uMJkA7nU.title: A Talk on Hajj: Walking in the Footsteps of Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad
908uMJkA7nU.one_line: On the eve of Arafah he reads the rites of Hajj symbolically, as retracing the stories of Adam and Hawwa, Ibrahim's family, and the Prophet.
908uMJkA7nU.summary: On the night before Arafah he sets fiqh aside and explains the symbolism of Hajj, which looks strange if seen only as travelling to stones in a desert. After arguing that repeating Hajj yearly is now nearly forbidden because it takes another Muslim's place, and that Hajj is devotional yet carries purposes, he names four levels. The highest is Ja'far al-Sadiq's: Arafah is Allah's door, the Haram His veil, the Ka'bah His house. The other three are paths. In Adam and Hawwa's footsteps, Arafah is where they recognized each other and where humanity's covenant was taken, Muzdalifah where they drew near and repented, Mina where they hoped and stoned Iblis, and the Ka'bah the house they built; ihram recalls their simplicity and the shroud, curing the love of immortality and power behind every evil. In Ibrahim's family's footsteps, Arafah is where he told Isma'il, Muzdalifah where Hajar joined, the jamarat where each stoned Iblis, and the sacrifice a celebration that Allah commands only what benefits us; Hajar's sa'y teaches that our duty is effort whatever the outcome. In the Prophet's footsteps, Arafah is where the religion was completed and jahiliyyah ended, Muzdalifah where he united his companions, Mina where his da'wah began.

outline.heading: Opening
Hajj seen mechanically versus symbolically
outline.gist: Seen physically, Hajj is walking among stones at great cost; understood symbolically, one longs to go every year.

outline.heading: Why repeating Hajj is now nearly forbidden
outline.gist: With two billion Muslims and room for three million pilgrims, a repeat Hajj takes someone else's only chance and risks lives in crowds.

outline.heading: Devotional acts that still have purposes
outline.gist: Like wudu after passing wind, Hajj is performed even without grasping its reason, yet it carries meanings people of insight perceive.

outline.heading: Four levels of Hajj
outline.gist: Three levels can be grasped by all; the fourth is understood only by those close to Allah.

outline.heading: Ja'far al-Sadiq: Arafah as the door, the Haram as the veil
outline.gist: Asked by Sufyan al-Thawri why Arafah lies outside the Haram, he said the pilgrims stand at Allah's door, are admitted to His veil, then visit His house, and guests do not fast.

outline.heading: Three paths and why Hajj is once in a lifetime
outline.gist: Hajj in the footsteps of Adam, Ibrahim or Muhammad; unlike any other worship it is once, bound to a place and time, to make you understand the story you belong to.

outline.heading: Adam's two weaknesses: fear of death and desire for dominion
outline.gist: Honoured and provided for in the Garden, Adam disliked being a servant who would die, and Iblis exploited this with the tree of eternity and lasting kingdom.

outline.heading: The fall: seeing his own flaws
outline.gist: Eating from the tree exposed not only their bodies but the flaws of his character; he was sent down to learn the worth of what he had.

outline.heading: Arafah, Muzdalifah and Mina in the story of Adam and Hawwa
outline.gist: Separated on earth, they recognized each other at Arafah, drew near at Muzdalifah, and at Mina wished to be better.

outline.heading: Jamrat al-Aqabah belongs to Adam
outline.gist: The three smaller jamarat are Ibrahim's story, but Aqabah is where Adam and Hawwa stoned Iblis.

outline.heading: The covenant at Na'man and Dawud's forty years
outline.gist: Allah drew Adam's offspring from his back near Arafah and took their testimony; Adam gave Dawud forty years then wanted them back, showing his fear of death.

outline.heading: Adam builds the first House
outline.gist: Commanded to build the House, Adam built it while Hawwa carried stones between Safa and Marwa, so every rite can retrace their steps.

outline.heading: Ihram as the dress of Adam
outline.gist: Two cloths, long hair and nails mirror our parents' first appearance; the name Adam means dark-skinned, as the first humans were.

outline.heading: Ihram as a shroud: Hajj cures love of life and power
outline.gist: Love of immortality and dominion gather every evil; Hajj reminds of death and tests humility among crowds, and arrogance ruins it.

outline.heading: Arafah: where the human story began
outline.gist: You return to where your parents met and where you testified that Allah is your Lord; Arafah carries the meaning of knowing.

outline.heading: Repentance at Muzdalifah and the meaning of haya'
outline.gist: Adam received the words 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves'; he fled out of shame, and haya' is the sensitivity that separates the living from the dead.

outline.heading: Knowledge, repentance, plan, resisting Iblis, obedience
outline.gist: Adam's path through the rites sums up the stages of a life, after which only death and Paradise remain, symbolized by leaving ihram.

outline.heading: Second path: Ibrahim and his family
outline.gist: Adam's story is a couple, Ibrahim's a family, the Prophet's a whole community.

outline.heading: Ibrahim returns to Isma'il at the age of striving
outline.gist: Isma'il, raised by Hajar near Zamzam and speaking Arabic, had reached the age when a son walks alongside his father.

outline.heading: The dream told at Arafah
outline.gist: Ibrahim told Isma'il of the dream at Arafah; studies of death-row prisoners show how unbearable such news is, yet Isma'il accepted.

outline.heading: Hajar joins at Muzdalifah
outline.gist: The mother who rarely saw her husband learned he would sacrifice her only son, and accepted once she knew it was Allah's command.

outline.heading: Iblis at the three jamarat
outline.gist: A family's obedience that could atone for the whole earth enraged Iblis, so each of them stoned him; only prophets see the unseen in this way.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the questioner did not question this command
outline.gist: He questioned the stars, idols and how Allah gives life, but asked nothing when told to sacrifice his son, and the knife was ordered not to cut.

outline.heading: The sacrifice celebrates that Allah commands only our benefit
outline.gist: Allah could have commanded what harms us, as with Ibrahim, but does not; like asking for only a fraction of wealth in zakat (47:36-38).

outline.heading: Tawaf: raising the House with Isma'il
outline.gist: Isma'il agreed to help his father build the House, praying for acceptance and for a messenger; tawaf walks in their steps.

outline.heading: The lost House and every prophet's Hajj
outline.gist: After Adam the House was washed away, yet every prophet performed Hajj there; Ibrahim was shown its place and told to call people to it.

outline.heading: Hajar's search between Safa and Marwa
outline.gist: Left with a little water, Hajar ran between the hills seven times watching her son, until Jibril struck the ground and Zamzam flowed.

outline.heading: Sa'y: your duty is effort, not the outcome
outline.gist: Zamzam did not come from her running, yet she had to strive; a Muslim never waits idly, since only those awaiting punishment wait.

outline.heading: Third path: the footsteps of the Prophet
outline.gist: Each place in Hajj has layers linking you to Allah, to Adam, to Ibrahim and to the final Prophet.

outline.heading: Arafah: the religion completed
outline.gist: With 5:3 revealed at Arafah the Prophet knew his mission was complete and his return to Allah near.

outline.heading: Jahiliyyah placed under his feet
outline.gist: At Arafah he abolished every matter of ignorance, starting with his own family's blood and riba; the days of ignorance ended and knowledge began.

outline.heading: Muzdalifah: gathering the companions
outline.gist: There he gathered, taught and prayed with his companions and warned them against division.

outline.heading: Mina: where his da'wah took root
outline.gist: In Mina he spent his years calling the pilgrims, until the youth of Yathrib responded.

outline.heading: Outro

3:139.ar: وَلَا تَهِنُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَوۡنَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
3:139.en: Faint not nor grieve, for ye will overcome them if ye are (indeed) believers

3:140.ar: إِن يَمۡسَسۡكُمۡ قَرۡحࣱ فَقَدۡ مَسَّ ٱلۡقَوۡمَ قَرۡحࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥۚ وَتِلۡكَ ٱلۡأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنكُمۡ شُهَدَآءَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
3:140.en: If ye have received a blow, the (disbelieving) people have received a blow the like thereof. These are (only) the vicissitudes which We cause to follow one another for mankind, to the end that Allah may know those who believe and may choose witnesses from among you; and Allah loveth not wrong-doers

3:141.ar: وَلِيُمَحِّصَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَيَمۡحَقَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
3:141.en: And that Allah may prove those who believe, and may blight the disbelievers

3:142.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَعۡلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَٰهَدُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَيَعۡلَمَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
3:142.en: Or deemed ye that ye would enter paradise while yet Allah knoweth not those of you who really strive, nor knoweth those (of you) who are steadfast

3:128.ar: لَيۡسَ لَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءٌ أَوۡ يَتُوبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَوۡ يُعَذِّبَهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
3:128.en: It is no concern at all of thee (Muhammad) whether He relent toward them or punish them; for they are evil-doers

3:133.ar: ۞وَسَارِعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
3:133.en: And vie one with another for forgiveness from your Lord, and for a paradise as wide as are the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who ward off (evil)

3:143.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ تَمَنَّوۡنَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَلۡقَوۡهُ فَقَدۡ رَأَيۡتُمُوهُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
3:143.en: And verily ye used to wish for death before ye met it (in the field). Now ye have seen it with your eyes

3:144.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولࣱ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُۚ أَفَإِيْن مَّاتَ أَوۡ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡقَٰبِكُمۡۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبۡ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَسَيَجۡزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
3:144.en: Muhammad is but a messenger, messengers (the like of whom) have passed away before him. Will it be that, when he dieth or is slain, ye will turn back on your heels? He who turneth back on his heels doth no hurt to Allah, and Allah will reward the thankful

3:145.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفۡسٍ أَن تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مُّؤَجَّلࣰ اۗ وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَا وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَاۚ وَسَنَجۡزِي ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
3:145.en: No soul can ever die except by Allah's leave and at a term appointed. Whoso desireth the reward of the world, We bestow on him thereof; and whoso desireth the reward of the Hereafter, We bestow on him thereof. We shall reward the thankful

33:14.ar: وَلَوۡ دُخِلَتۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۡ أَقۡطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةَ لَأٓتَوۡهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:14.en: If the enemy had entered from all sides and they had been exhorted to treachery, they would have committed it, and would have hesitated thereupon but little
