P1y5UXHGd_M.title: Between June 6th and Rafah: The Day After
P1y5UXHGd_M.one_line: On the day after the June 6 anniversary: what you do after a tragedy matters most, as Uhud's verses teach, with Dhul Hijjah a moment to decide.
P1y5UXHGd_M.summary: Speaking the day after the June 6 anniversary of the attack on a Muslim family in London, and at the start of Dhul Hijjah, he says he remembers the day after more than the day itself. The event was shock; the day after is when understanding comes and when the response is in your hands. He grounds this in the verses revealed after Uhud: do not weaken or grieve, days alternate among people, Allah tests and purifies the believers, did you think you would enter Paradise without striving, and Muhammad is only a messenger. For Gaza there is no day after yet, since Muslims have failed to stop the killing, but it will come and the question will be what its lessons did to us. He recalls a quiet moment in his youth when something he heard changed what he wanted to be, and says such moments are what you remember. The first ten days of Dhul Hijjah amplify every deed, including an intention to change. In the second khutbah he recalls the Prophet greeting the martyrs of Uhud, following them in purpose rather than in death, then asks how to prevent a repeat: politicians care only about votes, so Muslims must raise their voices and fund NCCM and their institutions so the next generation stands in better circumstances.

outline.heading: Opening
Gaza enters its ninth month
outline.gist: The first occasion behind the title: the attempted ethnic cleansing in Gaza enters its ninth month, with children losing grandparents, family and friends and growing up without safety, schooling or order.

outline.heading: I remember the day after more
outline.gist: The second occasion is the day after June 6. He remembers the day after the 2021 attack more than the day itself, which was turmoil and shock: who was driving, where, how could it happen.

outline.heading: The day after is yours
outline.gist: People speak of the day after a world war or any catastrophe because the event itself, good or terrible, is beyond your control; the day after is what you have in your hands to influence.

outline.heading: Uhud: 'not for you is the decision'
outline.gist: On the way back from Uhud the Prophet invoked curses on certain enemy leaders, and Allah revealed that the decision is not his, whether He forgives or punishes them (3:128). Then come the verses telling the believers not to weaken or grieve.

outline.heading: Days alternate; Allah tests and takes martyrs
outline.gist: If a wound touched you, a like wound touched them; such days Allah rotates among people so He knows the believers, takes martyrs from among them and purifies them (3:140-141).

outline.heading: Paradise without struggle?
outline.gist: Did you think you would enter Paradise, a life with no pain or difficulty, before Allah knows who strives and is patient (3:142)? You wished for death before you met it (3:143): this is how true believers handle the day after.

outline.heading: Muhammad is only a messenger
outline.gist: Muhammad is only a messenger, and messengers passed before him; would you turn back if he died? No soul dies except by Allah's leave, and each is given the reward of this world or the next that he seeks (3:144-145).

outline.heading: Gaza has no day after yet
outline.gist: For June 6 there is a day after; for Gaza there is not, because Muslims have failed to halt the killing and attempted genocide. It will end, as everything does, and the question will return.

outline.heading: A motionless moment that changed him
outline.gist: The day after, what will the lessons do for you? He recalls listening to someone as a young man and deciding who he wanted to be: nothing outward happened, no treaty signed, no applause, yet inside he said yes, I want to live like that.

outline.heading: The best ten days
outline.gist: Moments like that are what you remember. This day begins Dhul Hijjah: no days are greater or more beloved to Allah for good deeds, so increase tahlil, takbir and tahmid. Not even jihad compares, except a man who went out with his life and wealth and returned with nothing.

outline.heading: Everything is amplified, even an intention
outline.gist: That man vanished with no record he had lived, like the uncounted dead of today. We cannot match him, but we can come close by seizing these days, in which an intention to change our ways is amplified too.

outline.heading: Decide now what you will remember
outline.gist: As the day after, this is a good moment. He remembers how he felt on hearing that talk: no more empty living, he wanted to do something and be someone who cared. Decide now what you will look back on in fifteen or twenty years.

outline.heading: Interlude
Following the martyrs in purpose
outline.gist: Thinking of the dead of the Holy Land and of June 6, he recalls the Prophet greeting the martyrs of Uhud, Hamza, Mus'ab, Anas ibn al-Nadr and others, and vowing to follow them: not in death but in purpose, so their deaths would not be in vain.

outline.heading: The family taken from us
outline.gist: The Prophet promised the martyrs he would join them. The family taken on June 6 cannot be brought back, and attacks like it leave Muslims feeling unsafe walking down the street.

outline.heading: Politicians care only about votes
outline.gist: The community has barely discussed how to prevent another attack. Politicians do not care; they want your vote and will do anything to get it.

outline.heading: Fund our voice and institutions
outline.gist: To prevent a repeat, make Muslim voices louder and institutions stronger: fund NCCM properly and fund Muslim institutions so they can educate, teach and open their doors. If it happens again, you and I share the fault (33:14).

outline.heading: Keep climbing, keep fixing flaws
outline.gist: That is how it works: wherever you are, work to rise higher, keep looking at your flaws and fixing them, and keep working to protect the community from a repeat.

outline.heading: Leave them better circumstances
outline.gist: Ask how to stand for justice, strengthen Muslims' standing and improve the community's circumstances, so that when we are under the ground those standing here have better hopes and fewer fears. The day after is stepping back and making a decision you live by for the rest of your life.

outline.heading: Outro

18:9.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتَ أَنَّ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡكَهۡفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُواْ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا
18:9.en: Or deemest thou that the People of the Cave and the Inscription are a wonder among Our portents

18:10.ar: إِذۡ أَوَى ٱلۡفِتۡيَةُ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةࣰ وَهَيِّئۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَمۡرِنَا رَشَدࣰ ا
18:10.en: When the young men fled for refuge to the Cave and said: Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight

18:13.ar: نَّحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ نَبَأَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ إِنَّهُمۡ فِتۡيَةٌ ءَامَنُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ وَزِدۡنَٰهُمۡ هُدࣰ ى
18:13.en: We narrate unto thee their story with truth. Lo! they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance

18:14.ar: وَرَبَطۡنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ إِذۡ قَامُواْ فَقَالُواْ رَبُّنَا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَن نَّدۡعُوَاْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَٰهࣰ اۖ لَّقَدۡ قُلۡنَآ إِذࣰ ا شَطَطًا
18:14.en: And We made firm their hearts when they stood forth and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We cry unto no Allah beside Him, for then should we utter an enormity

18:22.ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةࣱ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمۡسَةࣱ سَادِسُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ رَجۡمَۢا بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبۡعَةࣱ وَثَامِنُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعۡلَمُهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱۗ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمۡ إِلَّا مِرَآءࣰ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا وَلَا تَسۡتَفۡتِ فِيهِم مِّنۡهُمۡ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:22.en: (Some) will say: They were three, their dog the fourth, and (some) say: Five, their dog the sixth, guessing at random; and (some) say: Seven, and their dog the eighth. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord is Best Aware of their number. None knoweth them save a few. So contend not concerning them except with an outward contending, and ask not any of them to pronounce concerning them

18:11.ar: فَضَرَبۡنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ فِي ٱلۡكَهۡفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدࣰ ا
18:11.en: Then We sealed up their hearing in the Cave for a number of years

18:12.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰهُمۡ لِنَعۡلَمَ أَيُّ ٱلۡحِزۡبَيۡنِ أَحۡصَىٰ لِمَا لَبِثُوٓاْ أَمَدࣰ ا
18:12.en: And afterward We raised them up that We might know which of the two parties would best calculate the time that they had tarried

18:15.ar: هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوۡمُنَا ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةࣰۖ لَّوۡلَا يَأۡتُونَ عَلَيۡهِم بِسُلۡطَٰنِۭ بَيِّنࣲۖ فَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا
18:15.en: These, our people, have chosen (other) gods beside Him though they bring no clear warrant (vouchsafed) to them. And who doth greater wrong than he who inventeth a lie concerning Allah

18:6.ar: فَلَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعࣱ نَّفۡسَكَ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمۡ إِن لَّمۡ يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡحَدِيثِ أَسَفًا
18:6.en: Yet it may be, if they believe not in this statement, that thou (Muhammad) wilt torment thy soul with grief over their footsteps

14:36.ar: رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضۡلَلۡنَ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِۖ فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّيۖ وَمَنۡ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
14:36.en: My Lord! Lo! they have led many of mankind astray. But whoso followeth me, he verily is of me. And whoso disobeyeth me - Still Thou art Forgiving, Merciful

5:118.ar: إِن تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ عِبَادُكَۖ وَإِن تَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
5:118.en: If Thou punish them, lo! they are Thy slaves, and if Thou forgive them (lo! they are Thy slaves). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Mighty, the Wise

e-NH_OrcWts.title: Activism, Our Path Forward 2: Youth and Belonging
e-NH_OrcWts.one_line: The cave youths show change needs few people but full commitment: young Muslims must act now and feel they belong to an ummah worth serving.
e-NH_OrcWts.summary: Bombs can destroy land and people but not ideas, he argues, and the ummah's real problem is not its enemies but that Muslims will not give their lives fully to the ideas they hold. So many Muslims agree on the basics and yet nothing changes, because commitment is missing. The People of the Cave were young, which is why this place exists: to tell young people they need not wait, need not be many, and that Allah will change the laws of nature for a few who make the cause their first priority. The youths likely doubted they could achieve anything and acted anyway; Allah raised them to show which idea outlasted the other, theirs or the tyrant's. Their second lesson is belonging: they called the misguided 'our people'. Young Muslims today do not feel they belong or matter, and the community must give them that. In the Arabic second khutbah he describes the Prophet as the true activist, who lost home, city, children and wealth and died with his armour in pawn, and tells how Umar wept at the mat's marks on his side. He ends with the Prophet weeping 'my ummah, my ummah' and urges school leavers to take this seriously and elders not to discourage them.

outline.heading: Ideas outlast bombs
outline.gist: Al-Kahf tells the story of a few activists who believed in an idea, and what stays is the idea. Israel can bomb land to oblivion, but destruction and killing only make an idea stronger in the hearts of those who hold it.

outline.heading: Our problem: ideas we will not give our lives to
outline.gist: The oppressors are up against an idea, and once its believers become its activists the story will end quickly. The ummah's problem is not relentless enemies but ideas it will not dedicate itself to fully; an idea only works at 100 percent.

outline.heading: So many of us, and nothing changes
outline.gist: There are so many Muslims agreeing on the basics, yet the world is still run by fascists, imperialists and colonialists who care for no one but themselves. What is missing is the commitment of the people.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:9: did you think it a wonder?
outline.gist: He loves how the story opens by confronting the reader: 'Did you think the people of the cave and the raqim were a wonder among Our signs?'

outline.heading: Youths who believed and were given more guidance
outline.gist: Whoever thinks Allah will not do again what He did for the people of the cave is mistaken. The youths took refuge in the cave; they were young men who believed in their Lord, were given more guidance, and had their hearts strengthened when they stood up.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:22: whatever their number, all young
outline.gist: People will say three and their dog, or five, or seven; whatever the number, all of them were young. That is why this place exists.

outline.heading: This place exists for the young
outline.gist: He established this place to speak to young people who are told, or led to believe, that impact is far off, that they still have time and are not ready yet.

outline.heading: A few companions are enough
outline.gist: You do not need many people with you; a few companions are enough for Allah to change how the laws of physics work for you. Are you willing to make the cause your first priority?

outline.heading: Nothing to wait for: all you have is now
outline.gist: The past cannot be changed and fades into a few snapshots by the time you are fifty. There is nothing to wait for; all you have in life is right now.

outline.heading: They doubted too, and acted anyway
outline.gist: Many think their numbers are too small; the youths thought exactly the same and were brave enough to live for an idea anyway. They likely told each other they could do almost nothing and still acted: you are obligated to do your best even when you doubt it will matter.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:12: which idea outlasted the other
outline.gist: Allah sealed their ears for years and raised them to see which party best reckoned their stay: which idea outlasted the other, that of three young men and their dog or that of the dictator with all the wealth and power.

outline.heading: Their declaration: our Lord is the Lord of the heavens
outline.gist: He recites their stand: they were youths who believed and were given more guidance, and when they stood up they said their Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and they would never call on any god besides Him.

outline.heading: 'These, our people' (18:15)
outline.gist: The second lesson is belonging. Activism needs people who feel they belong to a people worth serving, worth their time and dedication.

outline.heading: Young Muslims do not feel they belong
outline.gist: The youths still called those who took other gods 'our people'. Young Muslims today do not feel that; they want to sacrifice their time and energy but must first feel they belong to a nation they are proud of.

outline.heading: Make them feel they matter
outline.gist: It is not complicated: make sure young people feel they belong, are valued, matter and are part of something bigger than themselves. This is your generation of Muslims; you can complain about it all day or try something different.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet, an activist who lost everything
outline.gist: The English word activist describes the Prophet in every movement: he spared no effort serving Allah's servants. People revere him and forget that he lost his home, his city, his children, his wife and his wealth, and died with his armour pawned to a Jewish man.

outline.heading: No king; we lack youths like those of the cave
outline.gist: He was no king with people kissing his feet; he gave everything and returned to his Lord. The ummah lacks neither numbers nor money but youths like those of the cave, who strip themselves for the cause and ignore every voice that would turn them from it.

outline.heading: Umar and the mat: content with the Hereafter
outline.gist: Umar was finally admitted to the upper room where the Prophet had withdrawn from his wives, made him smile, and wept at the mat's marks on his side while Khosrau and Caesar lived in luxury. Rebuked with 'are you not content that they have this world and we the Hereafter?', Umar learned and lived as the Prophet did.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:6: grief that could destroy him
outline.gist: Allah told the Prophet he might almost destroy himself with grief over them if they did not believe: that is how much he gave of himself.

outline.heading: To those just out of school
outline.gist: He hopes the brothers and sisters who have just finished school take this to heart: the community is waiting for them and depending on them, and this place exists for them. Those who are older must not discourage them.

outline.heading: The Prophet recites Ibrahim's and Isa's prayers and weeps
outline.gist: Muslim narrates that he recited Ibrahim's words, 'whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, You are Forgiving, Merciful', and Isa's, 'if You punish them they are Your servants', then raised his hands and wept. Allah sent Jibril to ask why.

outline.heading: 'My ummah, my ummah'
outline.gist: He told Jibril, 'My ummah, my ummah'; no one today can hold a candle to that care. Allah sent Jibril back to say He would please him regarding his ummah and not grieve him.

outline.heading: A life to live and die by
outline.gist: Islam is far more profound than routine: something you live and die by. Bring young people back to the stories of the prophets and companions and they will see the beauty of that life and find a serenity found nowhere else.

outline.heading: Outro

28:35.ar: قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجۡعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلۡطَٰنࣰ ا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيۡكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآۚ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلۡغَٰلِبُونَ
28:35.en: He said: We will strengthen thine arm with thy brother, and We will give unto you both power so that they cannot reach you for Our portents. Ye twain, and those who follow you, will be the winners

28:36.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا بَيِّنَٰتࣲ قَالُواْ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ مُّفۡتَرࣰ ى وَمَا سَمِعۡنَا بِهَٰذَا فِيٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
28:36.en: But when Moses came unto them with Our clear tokens, they said: This is naught but invented magic. We never heard of this among our fathers of old

28:37.ar: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن جَآءَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ مِنۡ عِندِهِۦ وَمَن تَكُونُ لَهُۥ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
28:37.en: And Moses said: My Lord is Best Aware of him who bringeth guidance from His presence, and whose will be the sequel of the Home (of bliss). Lo! wrong-doers will not be successful

28:38.ar: وَقَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمۡتُ لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرِي فَأَوۡقِدۡ لِي يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ فَٱجۡعَل لِّي صَرۡحࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ أَطَّلِعُ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
28:38.en: And Pharaoh said: O chiefs! I know not that ye have a god other than me, so kindle for me (a fire), O Haman, to bake the mud; and set up for me a lofty tower in order that I may survey the god of Moses; and lo! I deem him of the liars

2:132.ar: وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعۡقُوبُ يَٰبَنِيَّ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
2:132.en: The same did Abraham enjoin upon his sons, and also Jacob, (saying): O my sons! Lo! Allah hath chosen for you the (true) religion; therefore die not save as men who have surrendered (unto Him)

4:54.ar: أَمۡ يَحۡسُدُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۖ فَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَآ ءَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُم مُّلۡكًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:54.en: Or are they jealous of mankind because of that which Allah of His bounty hath bestowed upon them? For We bestowed upon the house of Abraham (of old) the Scripture and wisdom, and We bestowed on them a mighty kingdom

4:55.ar: فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ ءَامَنَ بِهِۦ وَمِنۡهُم مَّن صَدَّ عَنۡهُۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيرًا
4:55.en: And of them were (some) who believed therein and of them were (some) who turned away from it. Hell is sufficient for (their) burning

5:23.ar: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمۡ غَٰلِبُونَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
5:23.en: Then out spake two of those who feared (their Lord, men) unto whom Allah had been gracious: Enter in upon them by the gate, for if ye enter by it, lo! ye will be victorious. So put your trust (in Allah) if ye are indeed believers

5:24.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَآ أَبَدࣰ ا مَّا دَامُواْ فِيهَا فَٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ
5:24.en: They said: O Moses! We will never enter (the land) while they are in it. So go thou and thy Lord and fight! We will sit here

5:25.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لَآ أَمۡلِكُ إِلَّا نَفۡسِي وَأَخِيۖ فَٱفۡرُقۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:25.en: He said: My Lord! I have control of none but myself and my brother, so distinguish between us and the wrong-doing folk

5:26.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡۛ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰۛ يَتِيهُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ فَلَا تَأۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:26.en: (Their Lord) said: For this the land will surely be forbidden them for forty years that they will wander in the earth, bewildered. So grieve not over the wrongdoing folk

7:171.ar: ۞وَإِذۡ نَتَقۡنَا ٱلۡجَبَلَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُۥ ظُلَّةࣱ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُۥ وَاقِعُۢ بِهِمۡ خُذُواْ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةࣲ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
7:171.en: And when We shook the Mount above them as it were a covering, and they supposed that it was going to fall upon them (and We said): Hold fast that which We have given you, and remember that which is therein, that ye may ward off (evil)

7:137.ar: وَأَوۡرَثۡنَا ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَانُواْ يُسۡتَضۡعَفُونَ مَشَٰرِقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَغَٰرِبَهَا ٱلَّتِي بَٰرَكۡنَا فِيهَاۖ وَتَمَّتۡ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْۖ وَدَمَّرۡنَا مَا كَانَ يَصۡنَعُ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَقَوۡمُهُۥ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡرِشُونَ
7:137.en: And We caused the folk who were despised to inherit the eastern parts of the land and the western parts thereof which We had blessed. And the fair word of thy Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their endurance; and We annihilated (all) that Pharaoh and his folk had done and that they had contrived

37:113.ar: وَبَٰرَكۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسۡحَٰقَۚ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحۡسِنࣱ وَظَالِمࣱ لِّنَفۡسِهِۦ مُبِينࣱ‏
37:113.en: And We blessed him and Isaac. And of their seed are some who do good, and some who plainly wrong themselves

3:21.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقࣲّ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
3:21.en: Lo! those who disbelieve the revelations of Allah, and slay the prophets wrongfully, and slay those of mankind who enjoin equity: promise them a painful doom

jjxMC7xxDr0.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas: Musa Before Pharaoh, Verses 35-38
jjxMC7xxDr0.one_line: Musa returns with clear proofs; Pharaoh answers with 'magic' and 'our forefathers', then dodges the debate through emotion, ridicule and deliberate delay.
jjxMC7xxDr0.summary: The sheikh opens by framing al-Qasas as a surah about human relationships, which are really relationships with each other's stories: we only ever see fragments, so we must not judge people by the part we witness, and should leave what does not concern us. He then recalls that Bani Israil, a people descended from prophets, lost their tawhid, identity and character under Pharaoh's enslavement and ignorance, and draws a direct parallel with Muslims after two centuries of tyranny and colonialism. Only a dedicated young generation, like Musa and Harun, can restore the ummah, and each generation must build into the next what it lacked. Moving through verses 35-38, he explains that prophets are promised an unbeatable proof, not personal safety. Pharaoh's reply rests on calling the miracles fabricated magic and appealing to ancestral custom, which he dissects with the legal principle of istishab: precedent applies only when no evidence exists. Musa's answer models Muslim objectivity: let evidence decide, because a Muslim has no fear of open debate. Pharaoh, bankrupt of argument, turns to emotional appeal, mockery of building a tower to look for Musa's God, and dragging the issue out until people lose interest. He urges patience before judging and readiness to argue from evidence.

outline.heading: Al-Qasas: relationships are made of each other's stories
outline.gist: We know people only through the stories told of them; lives cross briefly and then part.

outline.heading: You cannot judge a story from the fragment you see
outline.gist: Onlookers who saw Musa's mother cast him in the river, or Musa strike the man, would have judged wrongly; only Allah knows the whole story.

outline.heading: Leave what does not concern you
outline.gist: Help where you can, advise where you can, otherwise mind your own affairs; giving advice properly itself requires religious understanding, and intervening in others' private lives requires certainty and standing.

outline.heading: Recap: Musa's flight to Madyan and his wish to free his people
outline.gist: After the killing he went to Madyan, married and stayed about a decade, but returned still wanting to rescue Bani Israil, heirs of Yaqub's charge to die as Muslims.

outline.heading: Enslavement and ignorance strip a people of faith and identity
outline.gist: Bani Israil, descendants of prophets, lost their tawhid, honour and character under Pharaoh; only their young generation brought them back, which may be why Harun was given to Musa.

outline.heading: The Quran's objective treatment of Bani Israil
outline.gist: The Quran praises their virtues and names their sins without blanket condemnation, and this has no bearing on most people who call themselves Jews today.

outline.heading: Muslims today live what Bani Israil lived under Pharaoh
outline.gist: Two centuries of tyranny, colonialism and systematic ignorance have stripped the ummah of the generosity, courage and honour its grandparents inherited.

outline.heading: Only a dedicated youth can revive the ummah
outline.gist: Young people who devote themselves to the deen as Musa did are needed; Musa knew his people's faults and the Prophet held him up as the model of patience with them.

outline.heading: Forty years of wandering until a new generation arose
outline.gist: A generation that chooses to be useless cannot be forced to change; the wandering let that generation pass so a capable one could enter the holy land.

outline.heading: Each generation must build into the next what it lacked
outline.gist: This is not a call to discard elders; if every generation were worse there would be no point building masjids, so we invest in a coming generation to reclaim what was lost.

outline.heading: Musa returned mature, and Allah honoured his desire to reform
outline.gist: A young man's wish to rescue his people was rewarded with prophethood and direct speech from Allah; we hope for a share of that support.

outline.heading: Strengthening Musa with Harun and an unbeatable proof
outline.gist: Shadd al-'adud means support; the sultan is decisive evidence. Prophets are promised victory of their proof, not that they will not be killed, as Zakariyya and Yahya were.

outline.heading: The Prophet was given a proof that outlasts all others
outline.gist: Every prophet had an unbeatable sign for his era; the Prophet's sign, the Quran, remains for every era.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's first reply: fabricated magic
outline.gist: The confrontation with the sorcerers is compressed into one verse; iftira' means inventing with no basis, and Pharaoh brands the miracles a foreign, invented sorcery.

outline.heading: Musa's two calls and the ancestral excuse
outline.gist: Musa called to free Bani Israil and to tawhid; 'we never heard this from our forefathers' is the escape of one with no argument, used against Musa and Quraysh alike.

outline.heading: 'We have always done it this way' ruins religion, families and institutions
outline.gist: Holding to a practice only because of habit, in religion or any organisation, is among the most damaging answers to the question why.

outline.heading: Istishab: when precedent counts as evidence
outline.gist: Presumption of continuity is a recognised legal principle but ranks after Quran, Sunnah, consensus and analogy, as in eating animals the texts did not mention.

outline.heading: The Quranic reply: what if your fathers understood nothing?
outline.gist: Every person's practice is taken or left by evidence; al-Qasas skips the emotional scene of the sorcerers and focuses on the intellectual debate.

outline.heading: 'My Lord knows best who brought guidance'
outline.gist: Like the Prophet's 'either we or you are rightly guided' in Saba, Musa frames two claims that cannot both be true.

outline.heading: Check for common ground before arguing; stop Muslim infighting
outline.gist: Many disputes among Muslims are differences of terms and approach over one shared aim; they breed hatred and failure over things not worth it.

outline.heading: The one who seeks the truth earns the good end
outline.gist: Where claims truly clash, as tawhid against shirk, argue it out; whoever sincerely seeks the truth has the final abode even if he stumbles.

outline.heading: The wrongdoer never prevails: let evidence decide
outline.gist: Musa ignores Pharaoh's mockery and answers with facts, as in al-Shu'ara; resistance to change in any institution signals the lack of an argument.

outline.heading: A Muslim with clear proofs has nothing to fear
outline.gist: Only someone who fears his idea is weak dodges debate or tells people to stay away from others.

outline.heading: Muslim objectivity: bring your proof and I will follow it
outline.gist: A Muslim need not claim all truth or insult the other; the Quran itself says bring a better book and I will follow it, because there is no chance its proof is weaker.

outline.heading: A Muslim never follows blindly
outline.gist: Following is always on guidance, never blind imitation; Pharaoh, with nothing to put on the table, turns to political manoeuvring.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's emotional appeal: 'I know no god for you but me'
outline.gist: Faced with an objective opponent he cannot be openly partisan, so he plays the gentle, sincere ruler to win the crowd.

outline.heading: Allah still wanted Pharaoh to repent
outline.gist: Musa was told to speak gently; Pharaoh was his own enemy, as Umar would say; the Quran says he made light of his people and they obeyed.

outline.heading: Haman and firing the clay
outline.gist: Haman is a title like vizier, possibly linked to quarries; firing clay into stone may explain how the pyramids were built.

outline.heading: Aliens versus a Creator: modern credulity
outline.gist: People who mock belief in Allah readily believe aliens built the pyramids without any evidence; the stones were likely cast in place.

outline.heading: The tower to look for Musa's God
outline.gist: The sarh may have been a high observatory; Pharaoh knows it will show nothing and is mocking his people's intelligence.

outline.heading: Delay as a tactic: let the issue go cold
outline.gist: Dragging a heated issue out until people tire, as happened with Syria and Gaza; public attention lasts six to seven weeks before commitment fades.

outline.heading: Why Pharaoh could neither kill Musa nor debate him
outline.gist: Killing Musa would weaken him further and debating was hopeless, so a years-long building project bought time.

outline.heading: Preview: three verses compress everything up to the drowning
outline.gist: The nine signs and the exodus are summarised because the surah's focus is the argument between people.

outline.heading: A newcomer might side with Pharaoh
outline.gist: Seen from afar Pharaoh sounds reasonable and Musa an innovator, just as polished politicians fool people about their oppression.

outline.heading: Be patient before judging
outline.gist: You cannot even know what is presented to you, so hold back judgement.

COghj0V_PlY.title: Prophet Muhammad's Final Sermon
COghj0V_PlY.one_line: On the eve of Arafah, the Farewell Sermon's core: the sanctity of every Muslim's blood, wealth and honour and the equality of all people.
COghj0V_PlY.summary: Speaking the day before Arafah, he opens with the verse that perfected the religion, revealed at Arafah, then turns to Gaza, where the toll is climbing toward 37,000 and schools, hospitals and universities are bombed. It has not stopped, he says, because of the victims' skin, faith and language; Ukraine was handled very differently, and he is disgusted that academic institutions invest in the military. He walks through the Farewell Sermon: the Prophet before a vast crowd, his words relayed line by line, asking what day, month and land it was, and declaring blood, wealth and honour as sacred as that day, month and land, ending each point with 'have I conveyed?'. In the Arabic second khutbah he says one Muslim's blood outweighs the Kaaba, Arafah and every other sanctity combined, and had Muslims grasped this they would not be where they are. He adds the sermon's teaching that no race or colour is superior except by piety, and recalls a Ukrainian refugee saying this is not the Middle East. He warns of the Hawd, where some will be driven away for neglecting the Prophet's teaching, notes the Prophet left the world with nothing, and urges people to treat one another as sacred, fast Arafah and give their udhiyah.

outline.gist: He recites 'today I have perfected your religion' and the Bukhari report of a Jewish man telling Umar it deserved a festival, and Umar answering that he knew where and when it was revealed and where the Prophet was.

outline.heading: Gaza: the toll nears 37,000
outline.gist: Deaths keep climbing month after month as schools, hospitals and universities are bombed; it has not stopped only because of the victims' skin, faith and language.

outline.heading: Ukraine was handled differently
outline.gist: The world dealt with Ukraine very differently only months earlier, while governments and even academic institutions keep backing the Israeli military.

outline.heading: Universities that invest in the military
outline.gist: He can understand governments, but not institutions claiming integrity investing in a military because it is lucrative while it kills so many; children in the Holy Land cannot enjoy Eid without fear.

outline.heading: The day of Arafah
outline.gist: The best dua is the dua of Arafah: la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd. He turns to the Prophet's farewell Hajj.

outline.heading: After completion comes decline
outline.gist: Everything that is completed begins to decline, so the verse of completion came as his time drew near; he came to guide and lead, and addressed a vast crowd.

outline.heading: A sermon relayed through the crowd
outline.gist: People spread through the crowd repeated each passage so it could reach everyone, so the sermon took half an hour to an hour, with a question at the end of each passage.

outline.heading: 'I may not meet you after this year'
outline.gist: He opened by asking people to listen and understand, for he did not know whether he would meet them again in this place after this year.

outline.heading: 'What day is this?'
outline.gist: He asked what day it was and stayed silent until the companions thought he would rename it; they said Allah and His Messenger know best, and he named the day, then asked the same of the month.

outline.heading: A sacred month in a sacred land
outline.gist: It is a sacred month, and the land is Makkah, a sacred land.

outline.heading: Your blood, wealth and honour are sacred
outline.gist: Your blood, wealth and honour are as sacred to one another as this day, in this month, in this land; have I conveyed? The crowd answered yes.

outline.heading: One life above every sanctity
outline.gist: He called Allah to witness and made clear before he died that one human life is more sacred than any holy place, unlike what has been done for months.

outline.heading: Twenty years after he was cursed by his own
outline.gist: Every innocent life taken unjustly counts. Twenty years earlier his own people cursed him and tried to kill him, take his home and harm his companions; now he stood surrounded by followers to declare life sacred.

outline.heading: Interlude
His final will after twenty years of struggle
outline.gist: His words need no explanation: knowing his death was near, he stood surrounded by the Ansar and Muhajirun two decades after being reviled from a similar stand, and chose what to leave as his will.

outline.heading: One Muslim's blood outweighs the Kaaba
outline.gist: Had Muslims understood his will they would not have fallen; the blood, honour and wealth of a single Muslim are more sacred than the Kaaba, Arafah, Jumuah, Dhul Hijjah and Hajj combined.

outline.heading: 'Have I conveyed? O Allah, bear witness'
outline.gist: An ummah that grasped this could not end up where we are. He made them bear witness so that, asked on the Day of Judgment whether he forgot to warn them before they killed even children, women and the elderly, he can say he conveyed it.

outline.heading: No Arab over non-Arab, no white over black
outline.gist: Your Lord is one and your father is one, all from Adam and Adam from dust; no one is better except by taqwa, and the most honoured with Allah is the most righteous.

outline.heading: One human race
outline.gist: Remember the basics: humanity is one race and one family, beginning from one father.

outline.heading: Even oppressors are family
outline.gist: Even among us there are oppressors, transgressors and people without ethics, yet they are still part of the family, brothers and sisters.

outline.heading: Why is darker skin cheaper blood?
outline.gist: Why does some blood seem valuable and other blood not, with less value the darker the skin? That is the reality leaders and people live by.

outline.heading: 'This is not the Middle East'
outline.gist: A Ukrainian refugee interviewed in a subway said this was unacceptable because they are not the Middle East, as if people dying there or in Africa were normal. He then begins the hadith of the Hawd.

outline.heading: At the Hawd: do not blacken my face
outline.gist: He will precede his ummah to the Hawd and boast of their numbers before the nations, so do not embarrass him on that day; he will save some from the Fire, and some will be taken from him.

outline.heading: 'You do not know what they did after you'
outline.gist: He will call them his companions, and be told he does not know what they introduced after him.

outline.heading: How little they cared to learn his teachings
outline.gist: The phrase is usually applied to innovation, and he agrees, but zooms out: it also means how little they cared about his teachings and how little time they spent learning what he stood for.

outline.heading: He left the world with nothing
outline.gist: After all he showed them, they did not live as he explained; he entered and left the world with nothing, gave everything away, and pawned his own shield to pay someone else's debt.

outline.heading: Days for deciding how you will live
outline.gist: His shield had to be bought back after his death. Use these days to decide how you will live, so that you reach him at the Hawd and are not pulled away; taking each other's sanctity seriously would change our community.

outline.heading: If I saw your honour as sacred
outline.gist: He would treat others with more care, kindness and compassion, and what happens overseas would not happen. Tomorrow is Arafah: fast, spend it in dua and Quran, and offer the udhiyah here or for suffering Muslims abroad.

outline.heading: Outro
